events.name: Collectors Showcase
events.style: Rare cards, comics and memorabilia under one roof
events.whyGo: A low-priced, single-focus fair for rare cards, comics and memorabilia, in the smaller National Hall rather than Olympia's main show floor.
events.opNote: In the National Hall.

events.name: Winter Market at the Museum of the Home
events.style: A one-day makers' market of over 50 independent makers, small businesses and vintage sellers across the museum
events.price: Pay what you can; early access £8
events.whyGo: The museum becomes a gift market with artisanal homewares and seasonal presents from more than 50 independent sellers.
events.opNote: Saturday 28 November, 11am to 4pm, with early access from 10am for £8.

events.name: Winston Churchill: The Painter
events.style: A major retrospective of Churchill's paintings
events.whyGo: The side of Churchill almost nobody associates with him, in a townhouse museum that rarely runs ticketed shows at all.
events.opNote: The permanent Wallace Collection around it stays free.

events.name: Declaring Independence: USA 250
events.style: 250 years of American independence through the museum's collections
events.whyGo: Free and timed to the US semiquincentennial - a different angle for American visitors than the museum's ancient-world halls.
events.opNote: Pairs with the ticketed Bayeux Tapestry loan in the same building from September.

events.name: The Ideal Christmas Show
events.style: Christmas shopping show, run alongside the Cake & Bake Show
events.whyGo: Festive shopping, workshops and Santa's grotto at Olympia, open until 8pm on Thursday.

events.name: Mexican Christmas Market at Coal Drops Yard
events.style: A weekend market of Mexican crafts, ornaments and street food outside El Pastor, with a Norteño band and mariachi
events.address: Coal Drops Yard, outside El Pastor
events.whyGo: Seventh edition of a market curated by Paola Feregrino, with Mexican crafts, ornaments, clothing and jewellery, and sopes, tamales, churros, pan dulce and hot chocolate to eat. There are piñatas for families on Saturday and mariachi on Sunday.
events.opNote: Friday 27 to Sunday 29 November, 11am to 7pm each day. Saturday: piñata for families at 2pm, Mariachi El Mexicano with This is Mexico Dance Group at 3pm, piñata for all at 5pm. Sunday: mariachi at 1pm.

events.name: Christmas Fair at Chelsea Physic Garden
events.style: Over 100 independent and small businesses selling gifts inside London's oldest botanic garden
events.price: £8 booked in advance, £10 on the door
events.whyGo: More than 100 independent traders selling homewares, clothing, accessories, artisan food and drink, in London's oldest botanic garden.
events.opNote: Thursday 26 to Saturday 28 November 10am to 5pm; Sunday 29 November 10am to 4pm. Free for Friends of the Garden; guests of Friends must buy a ticket to the Fair.

events.name: Trafalgar Square Christmas Tree
events.style: Norway's annual thank-you gift, lit in early December with carols after
events.typicalWhen: Lighting ceremony in the first days of December; carols on the square most evenings until Christmas
events.whyGo: Norway has sent this tree every year since 1947 as thanks for wartime support - a real, continuous piece of diplomacy rather than decoration, usually lit by the Norwegian ambassador. Carol groups sing beneath it most December evenings, unticketed.
events.opNote: The 2026 tree is lit on Thursday 3 December. Carol groups sing beneath it most evenings until Christmas Eve.

events.name: England Women v Ukraine
events.style: FIFA Women's World Cup 2027 European qualifying play-off, second leg
events.price: Adults £15 to £59; under-16s, students and seniors £5 to £17.50
events.whyGo: England, the 2025 European champions, host the second leg at Wembley with a place at the 2027 World Cup finals in Brazil at stake.
events.opNote: Kick-off 5.30pm. Official tickets come through Wembley Stadium and Ticketmaster only. No under-2s are admitted.

events.name: Cinderella on Ice at Alexandra Palace
events.style: A Cinderella pantomime on ice performed by the rink's amateur skaters
events.whyGo: The cast are the skaters who train at the Alexandra Palace rink throughout the year, presented by Alexandra Palace Ice Rink Amateur Productions.
events.opNote: Six public performances: Thursday 3 and Friday 4 December at 7pm; Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 December at 1pm and 5.30pm. Suitable for children aged 3 and over.

events.name: Christmas at Summit: Alexandra Palace roof tour
events.style: A festive guided tour of the Palace roof, 130 metres above sea level, with a hot chocolate and mince pie
events.whyGo: A guided walk on the roof with panoramic views over London's skyline, by day, at sunset or after dark, with a free hot chocolate and mince pie.
events.opNote: Six dates: Friday 27 to Sunday 29 November and Friday 4 to Sunday 6 December. Doors open 9.45am, tours start at 10am, and tickets are sold by time slot. Minimum age 8. Meet in the East Court.

events.name: Christmas Fair at Eltham Palace
events.style: A weekend of artisan stalls in the medieval Great Hall, with marshmallow toasting in the gardens
events.whyGo: Local makers sell jewellery, pottery and artwork in the medieval Great Hall, and children and adults can toast marshmallows outside. A wreath trail runs through the gardens and free garden tours run through the day.
events.opNote: Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 December, 10am to 4pm. Included with admission; English Heritage members get free entry; booking in advance saves 15%.

events.name: The Tale of a Winter Whale at Hall Place and Gardens
events.style: An after-dark lantern-lit trail through the gardens telling a story of Neptune, mermaids and pirates, by outdoor-arts company Same Sky
events.whyGo: A lantern-lit walk from tropical waters to icy Arctic seas, with glowing sea creatures and costumed characters. A free four-day festive market runs alongside.
events.opNote: Thursday 3 to Sunday 6 December, evening sessions from 4pm on Thursday; the last session on Sunday ends at 9.30pm. Suitable for all ages. The Festive Market is free, with no ticket needed: 4pm to 9pm on 3 and 4 December, 12pm to 9pm on 5 and 6 December.

events.name: Beautiful & Useful Craft Fair at the Garden Museum
events.style: A one-day fair of designer-makers selling ceramics, textiles, prints, jewellery and homewares
events.price: £5; free for Friends and Young Fronds
events.whyGo: Stallholders include embroiderer Megan Ivy Griffiths, printmaker Sophie Elm, jeweller Lucy Behrens and stained-glass artist Harriet Love, and workshops include fair entry.
events.opNote: Sunday 6 December, 10am to 4pm.

events.name: London International Animation Festival 2026
events.style: Ten days of animation screenings, talks and events across the Barbican, The Garden Cinema, The Horse Hospital and other venues
events.whyGo: A BAFTA-qualifying festival with international competition programmes, a stop-motion panorama and sessions for children from 0 to 15.
events.opNote: 27 November to 6 December. Barbican screenings are £14 standard (opening night and Best of the Fest £16); The Garden Cinema £15, The Horse Hospital £10, Close-Up Cinema £12. Late Night Bizarre at The Horse Hospital is 18+. A VIP online pass is £79.

events.name: Yamaha Presents: The Moonlight Concert at Sky Garden
events.style: Five-piece orchestra playing modern classics and Christmas songs by candlelight
events.price: £25 standing with a glass of Moët; tables £45 to £65
events.whyGo: Hundreds of candles, a five-piece orchestra and the skyline at night, on two evenings only.
events.opNote: Two nights: Monday 16 November and Tuesday 8 December (the Christmas edition). Standing access includes a glass of Moët; table prices include a sharing platter.

events.name: A Christmas Carol at Highgate Cemetery
events.style: A one-man telling of A Christmas Carol by storyteller Jason Buck, among the Victorian graves
events.whyGo: Jason Buck tells the story live, as Dickens intended it, in the surroundings of Highgate Cemetery.
events.opNote: One night: Thursday 10 December 2026.

events.name: London Perfume Exhibition
events.style: Fragrance trade platform with a public 'passionate visitors' day
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: This is the first edition of this fragrance show in London, mixing a trade platform with a public 'passionate visitors' day rather than running trade-only.
events.opNote: Only part of the run is open to the public - check which days before booking.

events.name: Lower Stable Street Christmas Market
events.style: A Christmas run of the B Corp-certified Lower Stable Street Market, with street food, crafts, clothing and gifts
events.venue: Coal Drops Yard, Lower Stable Street
events.address: Lower Stable Street, Coal Drops Yard
events.whyGo: Independent traders selling street food, drinks, crafts and clothing on the weekends before the Shōtengai market takes over, so Lower Stable Street has a market every weekend until 20 December.
events.opNote: Thursday to Sunday, 26 to 29 November and 10 to 13 December, 11am to 6pm.

events.name: The Film London Jarman Award 2026
events.style: Films by the four artists shortlisted for the 2026 Jarman Award: Sadia Pineda Hameed, Ilona Sagar, Rhea Storr and Alia Syed
events.whyGo: Four shortlisted artists' films showing the range of artists' filmmaking in the UK, free to see in one gallery.
events.opNote: Tuesday 17 November to Sunday 13 December. Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 11am to 6pm; Thursday 11am to 9pm; closed Mondays.

events.name: North Yard Festive Nights at Camden Market
events.style: Thursday-night festive markets in North Yard with a live brass band and mulled drinks
events.venue: Camden Market, North Yard and Stables
events.whyGo: Mulled drinks on the cobbles with the Bavarian Strollers brass band playing festive favourites, and Christmas menus at the North Yard restaurants: Igra Rama, Ester, Epicurus, Hans & Gretel, Humble Crumble and Pick & Cheese.
events.opNote: Four Thursdays, 26 November, 3, 10 and 17 December, 5.30pm to 9pm. Live brass band throughout the evening.

events.name: Museum by Candlelight at The Fan Museum
events.style: Five late evenings in a Georgian house lit almost entirely by candles
events.whyGo: The museum opens late for five evenings with its exhibition spaces lit almost entirely by candles, classical festive music, and a complimentary mulled wine, cider or juice in the Orangery.
events.opNote: 4.30pm to 7pm. Tickets must be booked in advance; none are sold on the door.

events.name: The Waldorf Project: Chapter Five / KAIHOGYO
events.style: Long-form sensory art
events.whyGo: A sustained sensory work rather than a show with a running time - the Waldorf Project's chapters are closer to endurance art than theatre.
events.opNote: Runs 19 November to 20 December 2026. Over-18, and demanding by design - not a casual evening out.

events.name: Shōtengai Pan-Asian Christmas Market at Coal Drops Yard
events.style: Lower Stable Street dressed as a Japanese shōtengai, a local street market, with pan-Asian food and crafts
events.venue: Coal Drops Yard, Lower Stable Street
events.address: Lower Stable Street, Coal Drops Yard
events.whyGo: Shōtengai are the covered local street markets found across Japanese cities; this festive edition fills Lower Stable Street with pan-Asian food and crafts from small independent traders.
events.opNote: Two runs: Thursday 3 to Sunday 6 December and Thursday 17 to Sunday 20 December. Thursday and Friday 12pm to 7pm; Saturday and Sunday 11am to 6pm.

events.name: Father Christmas at Kenwood
events.style: A group story session in the Old Kitchen followed by meeting Father Christmas, with a present for each child
events.price: £15 per child, £12 for English Heritage members
events.whyGo: A storytelling session in the Old Kitchen in the Service Wing, then a meeting with Father Christmas with a chance for photographs. Each child gets a traditional present to unwrap.
events.opNote: Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November, then weekends from Saturday 5 to Sunday 20 December. Sessions at 10.20am, 11am, 11.40am, 12.20pm, 1.40pm, 2.20pm and 3pm. One accompanying adult per child; every child needs a ticket. Arrive 15 minutes early. Step-free access.

events.name: Festive Fun at Eltham Palace and Gardens
events.style: A family Christmas quest trail through the grounds of the Art Deco house, with Father Christmas for an extra charge
events.whyGo: Families follow Ellie and Jack's Christmas Quest trail around the grounds; the trail is included in entry.
events.opNote: Weekends only, Saturday 5 to Sunday 20 December, 10am to 4pm. There is an extra charge to visit Father Christmas. English Heritage members get free entry; booking in advance saves 15% and guarantees entry.

events.name: London International Horse Show
events.style: Traditional Christmas showjumping fixture
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: A traditional Christmas showjumping fixture, now run at ExCeL rather than its old Olympia home.

events.name: Remixed Roller Skating Rink at King's Cross
events.style: A roller-skating rink in Lewis Cubitt Square with DJ takeovers and roller discos, in place of the usual ice rink
events.price: £12 weekdays, £14.95 weekends; under-8s skate free with a paying adult
events.whyGo: Roller skates instead of ice skates, set to festive hits. Lightroom runs Bowie-inspired sessions on four Fridays and Queer Britain has a Saturday set from Ella Vaday.
events.opNote: 11am to 8pm daily; sessions last 45 minutes and the last starts at 7pm. Minimum skating age is 5, and an adult must accompany under-12s. Skate Skool at 11am daily; low-sensory sessions at 12pm on Wednesdays and Sundays; the 7pm session is adults only (18+). £1 from every ticket goes to New Horizon Youth Centre.

events.name: 12 Nights of Christmas at Sky Garden
events.style: Festive live band, DJ, jazz and candlelit music nights in the Sky Pod Bar, 35 floors up
events.typicalWhen: Mid November to just before Christmas
events.whyGo: A paid evening ticket into Sky Garden with a welcome drink, live bands and DJs, and the garden lit for Christmas. It gets you in when the free viewing slots have gone.
events.opNote: Two standing sessions a night, 18:30 to 20:45 and 20:45 to 22:45. Theme nights: Step Into Christmas parties 20 and 27 November, Moët Christmas parties 5, 12, 19, 22 and 23 December, the Big Christmas Party 11 and 18 December, Festive Jazz Club 15 December. Strictly 18+ with physical photo ID; cashless.

events.name: Christmas Under the Canopy at King's Cross
events.style: A covered Christmas market of artisan traders and food stalls under festive lights, with live music
events.whyGo: A covered market that opens earlier in the week and later into the evening for Christmas, with designer-makers, original crafts and street food traders under the canopy.
events.opNote: Tuesday to Sunday, 20 November to 23 December, plus Monday 21 December. Tuesday and Wednesday 12pm to 7pm; Thursday and Friday open until 8pm; weekends from 11am.

events.name: Real Food Christmas Markets at King's Cross and London Bridge
events.style: Station-side Christmas markets of independent food traders, mulled wine and gifts in chalets and under railway arches
events.venue: King's Cross Square, London Bridge Station and Euston Station
events.whyGo: Street food, mulled wine and gifts at stations you are passing through anyway: chalets outside King's Cross, and makers' stalls under the arches inside London Bridge Station on Stainer Street.
events.opNote: Daily 11am to 7pm. King's Cross Square and Euston Station run 24 November to 23 December; London Bridge runs 23 November to 23 December.

events.name: Santa's Grotto at Alexandra Palace
events.style: A five-minute visit to Santa's grotto in the East Court, with a small gift
events.whyGo: Children meet Santa, get a small gift and a photo opportunity in his grotto, with Christmas trees, lights and carols in the East Court around it.
events.opNote: 4 to 23 December. One under-16 ticket admits up to two adults. Sessions last five minutes. A 6x4 photo print is £15.

events.name: Christmas Festival at Smith Square Hall
events.style: Three weeks of Christmas concerts by orchestras, choirs and soloists in a Baroque church
events.whyGo: A run of seasonal concerts including Handel's Messiah on Friday 4 December at 7pm, Roderick Williams in Schubert's Winterreise on Sunday 6 December, NYJO Blueprint orchestra in Ellington's Nutcracker on 7 December and a gospel choir on 11 and 12 December.
events.opNote: 2 to 23 December. Prices are set per concert on each listing. Libera in Concert on 5 December is sold out.

events.name: Wundrful World Of Christmas
events.style: Immersive meet-Santa experience
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: Meet Santa and his Elves inside a full immersive Christmas build, running six weeks rather than a single weekend.

events.name: Winter Adventure at Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
events.style: A free daily programme of performances, workshops and festive activities, with a different Park venue opening its door each day
events.whyGo: Every day from 1 to 24 December a different venue in the Park opens its door to a free performance, activity or celebration, which the Park calls a living advent calendar. The first evening is carols and family badminton at Copper Box Arena.
events.opNote: Tuesday 1 to Thursday 24 December. All events are free and open to everyone. Most need no booking; the few that do ask for free registration on their listing.

events.name: The Sea Star Search with the Elf on the Shelf at SEA LIFE London
events.style: An elf-led activity trail around the aquarium to recover missing decorations for the Undersea Christmas Tree
events.whyGo: Children collect an activity sheet on entry, solve challenges at each interactive point and earn a piece of the Christmas Sea Star, then a certificate.
events.opNote: 1 to 24 December, included with admission at your chosen time slot. Booking online in advance is cheaper than the door price.

events.name: Santa's Grotto and the Snow Queen at the Queen's House
events.style: An actor-led story adventure through the Queen's House, based on the Snow Queen, ending at Santa's Grotto
events.price: £30 per person, £27 for Family Members, under-1s free, plus £3 booking fee per transaction
events.whyGo: Children follow the Snow Queen, her assistant the Hobgoblin, Gerda, Kai and the little robber girl through a 17th-century royal house dressed in white trees and icy blue lights, then meet Father Christmas and take a gift home.
events.opNote: Saturday 14 November to Thursday 24 December. Booked time slots; relaxed sessions are listed separately.

events.name: Christmas at Chessington World of Adventures
events.style: A Christmas Village with Father Christmas's grotto, a pantomime, carollers and selected theme-park rides
events.price: From £32 per person; short breaks from £62 per person
events.whyGo: A theme-park day with a festive layer: a Christmas Village Passport takes children through an elf welcome, letters to Father Christmas, a silent disco and a snowy woodland to the grotto, and this year's pantomime is Cinderella.
events.opNote: Selected dates between 21 November and 24 December; book early for the best availability. The Christmas Village closes on 24 December, though Twixmas runs at the park until 3 January.

events.name: Duck Pond Festive Market at Chiswick House
events.style: A Sunday-style market of local, ethical independent businesses in the gardens, with street food and a café
events.whyGo: Local, ethical and sustainable small businesses selling gifts, crafts, plants and seasonal food in the gardens, with coffee from the café.
events.opNote: 10am to 4pm on 5 and 6 December, 19 and 20 December, and 21 to 24 December (the 1 November date has passed).

events.name: The Peter Pan Cup
events.style: The Serpentine club's Christmas morning race in an unheated lake
events.whyGo: Serpentine Swimming Club members race across open cold water on Christmas morning while the rest of the park watches in coats - named for the Peter Pan statue nearby and run since 1864. One of the only things happening in London on the day itself.
events.opNote: Spectating is free and unticketed; swimming is members-only with qualifying swims through the winter. Mid-morning by the Lido.

events.name: Scrooge: Cirque Extravaganza
events.style: Festive circus and theatre show
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.price: From £23-28 off-peak per ticket, minimum 4 for family pricing
events.whyGo: A festive circus and theatre retelling of A Christmas Carol, timed for the days right before Christmas.
events.opNote: Family pricing needs a minimum of four tickets.

events.name: London New Year's Eve Fireworks
events.style: The midnight fireworks fired from the London Eye - ticketed, not walk-up
events.venue: The Thames between Westminster and the Eye
events.whyGo: The Mayor's display over the Thames at midnight, watched from six fenced, ticketed viewing areas along the river. It has been ticketed since 2014, and there is no walk-up entry.
events.opNote: Tickets come only through the link on london.gov.uk, up to four per buyer, £20 to £55. They were released in two batches, the second and final one at 12 noon on Friday 20 November 2026. There are no official viewing areas in any Royal Park, and Primrose Hill is locked overnight.

events.name: New Year's Eve at Sky Garden
events.style: All-night party with DJs, a live band and the midnight fireworks seen from 35 floors up
events.whyGo: A view over the whole skyline for the midnight fireworks, without standing on the Embankment.
events.opNote: Party access from £220 includes a glass of Moët and roaming canapés; a bar table with a sharing platter is from £290. Dinners that include the party: Fenchurch from £795, Darwin Brasserie from £465. Larch's set menu from £120 can add party access.

events.name: White Christmas at Seven Dials Market
events.style: Indoor snowfall twice a day in a Covent Garden food hall, with Baileys cocktails and festive specials from the traders
events.whyGo: Snow falls inside the market every day at 3pm and 8pm. Thirteen traders have festive specials, including a cheeseboard pizza from Bad Boy Pizza Society and profiteroles with a party popper of pine-flavoured edible snow from Chin Chin and Mello.
events.opNote: 12 November to 31 December. Baileys happy hour every day at 8pm; live music every Friday and Saturday from 7pm.

events.name: Concrete and Clay: Archiving the Barbican
events.style: The estate's own architectural history, free
events.whyGo: The Brutalist estate explaining itself - the best primer before wandering the highwalks, and it closes for good on New Year's Day 2027 despite feeling permanent.
events.opNote: Free, inside the Centre; combine with the conservatory's Sunday openings.

events.name: London New Year's Day Parade
events.style: 8,000 performers parade Piccadilly to Parliament Square every 1 January
events.typicalWhen: 1 January, every year, whatever the weather
events.address: Route from Piccadilly to Parliament Square
events.price: Free from the route; grandstands paid
events.whyGo: More than 8,500 performers - marching bands, cheerleaders, floats - walk the same 2.2-mile route every New Year's Day. One of the only major London events guaranteed to a fixed date you can build a trip around.
events.opNote: Free along the whole route; paid grandstand seats exist near Piccadilly. Runs 1pm to 4.30pm.

events.name: Southbank Centre Winter Market
events.style: Free-entry riverside Christmas market
events.typicalWhen: Early November to just after New Year
events.whyGo: The free-entry alternative to ticketed Winter Wonderland - chalets, food and mulled wine along the river with the Eye behind, walkable as part of a South Bank evening rather than an outing in itself.
events.opNote: No entry fee; you pay at the stalls. Busiest weekend evenings.

events.name: Hampton Court Palace Ice Rink
events.style: Skating against the Tudor palace facade
events.typicalWhen: Late November to the first weekend of January
events.whyGo: The most atmospheric rink in the London area for the Tudor backdrop alone, with adults-only evening sessions on selected dates. Christmas weekends sell out.
events.opNote: Dates from listings sites, not yet confirmed on the rink's own site - check before booking travel.

events.name: Leicester Square Christmas Market
events.style: Bavarian-style chalets in the West End
events.typicalWhen: Early November to just after New Year
events.whyGo: The central, no-ticket Christmas market, running the whole festive period. The chalet bar packages are the only ticketed part - the market itself costs nothing to enter.
events.opNote: Bar packages from about £26.50 book separately. Rammed on December weekends.

events.name: Frida: The Making of an Icon
events.style: How Kahlo's public image was constructed
events.whyGo: Framed around Kahlo's image-making rather than straight biography - a different show from the Kahlo retrospectives most people have already seen.
events.opNote: Runs through the Christmas peak; book the quiet January weekdays.

events.name: Peaky Blinders: Underworld
events.style: Walk-through Shelby underworld
events.whyGo: Starts in a rebuilt Garrison Tavern, then a hidden door drops you into the Shelby underworld to wander, meet actors and work things out for yourself.
events.opNote: In the railway arches at 8 Bermondsey Street - the aggregator files it under London Bridge, which sends people to the wrong side of the station.

events.name: Hyde Park Winter Wonderland
events.style: Christmas market, rides and ice rink
events.price: Timed entry ticket from £1; rides and rink extra
events.whyGo: Rides, bars, market stalls, shows and an ice rink across Hyde Park, from 19 November to 3 January.
events.opNote: Everyone needs a timed entry ticket, from £1 off-peak (Monday to Thursday in November); the rides and rink are paid separately and it adds up fast. Spend £25 online in one transaction and entry is free.

events.name: Christmas at Kew
events.style: After-dark illuminated trail through the gardens
events.typicalWhen: Mid-November to early January, after dark
events.whyGo: A 3km illuminated trail through Kew Gardens after dark, on selected evenings from 13 November 2026 to 3 January 2027.
events.opNote: Timed entry and it sells out weeks ahead, especially at weekends. Allow two hours or more outdoors in December - dress for it properly.

events.name: Paddy Power World Darts Championship 2026/27
events.style: PDC world title darts over 36 sessions, in the Great Hall for the first time
events.price: Tiered seats from £55, table seats from £75, 501 Club hospitality from £399
events.whyGo: The PDC world title runs for 36 sessions from Friday 11 December to Sunday 3 January, in the Great Hall for the first time, with room for over 5,000 a session.
events.opNote: Tickets were allocated by ballot, which has closed; any resale must go through See Tickets' Fan-to-Fan platform. Evening doors open at 7pm.

events.name: King's Cross Winter Market
events.style: Free-entry Christmas market in Granary Square, new for 2026
events.whyGo: A new market for 2026 with independent food, drink and makers' stalls, seasonal bars and a winter bandstand. It sits beside Aardman's Cracking Christmas Tree and the bookable Remixed Roller Rink, which runs 26 November to 22 December.
events.opNote: Until 23 December: Sunday to Thursday 11am to 10pm, Friday and Saturday 11am to 11pm. Closed 25 and 26 December and 1 January; 11am to 7pm on Christmas Eve.

events.name: Christmas at the Charles Dickens Museum
events.style: The historic house decorated for a Victorian Christmas, with readings of Dickens by candlelight through December
events.whyGo: The house where Dickens wrote Oliver Twist is dressed for a Victorian Christmas. James Swanton performs A Christmas Carol and other Dickens ghost stories on most evenings from 1 to 23 December, and there are magic lantern shows on 28 and 29 November.
events.opNote: Open 10am to 5pm with last entry at 4pm on most days; closed 25 and 26 December and 1 January. Admission tickets and event tickets are separate. On Christmas Eve only event ticket holders are admitted, for the Christmas Eve Special Opening, from £25.

events.name: Festive Flights on the London Eye
events.style: Decorated pods and a narrated Christmas story on a standard London Eye flight
events.address: Riverside Building, County Hall, Westminster Bridge Road
events.whyGo: Every London Eye ticket includes the festive flight: decorated pods and a guest narrator telling stories of Christmas in London past and present, over views of Big Ben, Buckingham Palace and St Paul's.
events.opNote: Included with all tickets for visits 14 November to 3 January. Extras: Santa in the Sky on selected dates in November and December; a Festive Champagne Flight with Moët & Chandon until 3 January; Festive Afternoon Tea until 23 December.

events.name: Shrek the Halls at Shrek's Adventure! London
events.style: A Christmas adventure added to the Shrek's Adventure! walk-through and 4D bus ride
events.price: Tickets from £21 per adult; included in entry
events.whyGo: The Christmas adventure is included with a standard ticket, so there is nothing extra to pay once you are in.
events.opNote: 5 December to 3 January. Pre-book online to guarantee entry. Under-2s go free.

events.name: Festive Skate at Alexandra Palace
events.style: Public ice skating beneath a Christmas tree, with festive music and falling snow
events.whyGo: An indoor rink under a tall Christmas tree, with mince pies, mulled wine and Baileys hot chocolate from the East Court Café afterwards.
events.opNote: 9 December to 4 January. Skaters must be 3 or over. Anyone supervising an under-16 who is not skating needs a spectator ticket.

events.name: Skate at Somerset House
events.style: The courtyard rink with the 40ft tree
events.whyGo: The most elegant of the central rinks - a working arts venue's courtyard rather than a fenced-off park - with late adult sessions alongside family daytimes.
events.opNote: Skate Lates evenings run DJ sessions; daytime is family territory. Book a slot type deliberately.

events.name: Justin Caguiat: Change Ringing
events.style: First UK institutional show for the painter
events.whyGo: A first UK institutional show spanning painting, sculpture, print, sound and film - genuine discovery rather than greatest hits, and free.
events.opNote: Amar Kanwar runs at Serpentine North across the bridge; one visit covers both.

events.name: The Music Is Black: A British Story
events.style: The history of Black British music, at the new V&A East
events.address: Stratford Waterfront, Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
events.whyGo: A flagship show at the brand-new V&A East, telling a specifically British story rather than importing an American music history.
events.opNote: V&A East is at Stratford, not South Kensington - a different building entirely.

events.name: Rising Voices: Contemporary Art from Asia, Australia and the Pacific
events.style: A broad regional survey
events.whyGo: Asia, Australia and the Pacific in one survey - broader than the V&A usually attempts, and £11 cheaper than its Schiaparelli headliner.
events.opNote: Works as the second show on a Schiaparelli visit.

events.name: Sophie's Surprise Christmas Party
events.style: Circus and comedy Christmas show
events.whyGo: Circus, cabaret and comedy in a Christmas show that is emphatically not for children, and returns most years.
events.opNote: Runs 13 November 2026 to 10 January 2027. Age 16 and over - the name is misleading and families do turn up expecting otherwise.

events.name: Christmas Silent Night at Dennis Severs' House
events.style: A silent 45-minute visit to a historic house in Spitalfields, lit only by candles and dressed for Christmas
events.whyGo: You walk through the house without speaking, in rooms lit by candles, with ticking clocks, crackling fires and the smell of woodsmoke and cloves.
events.opNote: Book a timed slot from the calendar, 20 November 2026 to 10 January 2027. Be punctual: latecomers cannot be admitted. Under-16s must be accompanied, one adult per child. Tickets are non-refundable and cannot be transferred. Steep stairs and uneven floors; no toilets, and only handbags and small backpacks are allowed in.

events.name: LAIKA presents Wildwood: The Exhibition
events.style: Original props, sketches, puppets and miniature sets from the stop-motion studio's film Wildwood
events.price: Adult from £15.29, concession from £11.47, child from £7.65
events.whyGo: Traces Wildwood from early ideas through character and environment design, puppet fabrication, rapid prototyping, miniature set construction and animation, from the Oregon studio behind Coraline and Kubo and the Two Strings.
events.opNote: 15 October 2026 to 10 January 2027. Tickets are non-refundable and non-exchangeable; members go free. Closed 24 to 26 December.

events.name: Salman Toor: Someone Like You
events.style: The first solo exhibition in Europe of the New York painter, with 19 paintings never shown in Britain
events.venue: Courtauld Gallery, Denise Coates Exhibition Galleries
events.whyGo: Paintings of friendship, love, solitude and alienation in queer and immigrant lives, from a painter whose figures live between cultures.
events.opNote: 2 October 2026 to 10 January 2027, 10am to 6pm, last entry 5.15pm. Friday late openings until 8pm on 4 December and 8 January. Courtauld Members go free; the exhibition is on floor 3 with lift access.

events.name: Ana Mendieta
events.style: Survey of the Cuban-American performance and land artist
events.whyGo: Mendieta's body-and-land work rarely gets a full London survey. Some pieces deal with violence against women - not a casual outing, and worth knowing before booking.
events.opNote: Content warnings apply; check Tate's guidance.

events.name: Zineb Sedira: When Words Fall Silent, Cinema Speaks
events.style: The Tate Britain Commission, filling the Duveen Galleries
events.whyGo: Free, and the annual Commission uses the Duveen Galleries at a scale no room-based show can. Sedira represented France at the Venice Biennale.
events.opNote: In the free central galleries - no ticket.

events.name: Johnstone's Paint Masters Snooker 2027
events.style: Invitation snooker for the world's top 16 players
events.price: From £35 a session, plus a 10% booking fee and a £2.10 restoration levy per ticket
events.whyGo: The Masters has been staged at Alexandra Palace since 2012, with a crowd of over 2,000 watching the world's top 16 players.
events.opNote: Doors open at 11:30. Sessions start at 1pm and 7pm and are provisional until World Snooker Tour confirms them. All seating is reserved. Matches are best of 11 frames until the final, which is best of 19. Under-16s must be with an adult over 21.

events.name: Freddie Mercury: Splendid Things
events.style: A free trail of eight Freddie Mercury looks spread across the museum, for his 80th anniversary year
events.whyGo: Eight looks spanning his career, from music videos to stage performances, placed across the museum so you find them as you walk round.
events.opNote: Closes Sunday 17 January 2027. Free, no booking required.

events.name: Yuko Mohri: In Concert
events.style: Kinetic sound work built for the Barbican's Curve
events.whyGo: Built specifically for the Curve's shape by an artist who represented Japan at Venice - site-responsive in the literal sense.
events.opNote: Price not on the listing - check when booking.

events.name: London Art Fair
events.style: Modern and contemporary galleries selling direct to visitors in Islington
events.price: Day ticket £27.75 in advance, £28 on the door; Wednesday Late £21.25; concessions £23.25
events.whyGo: Galleries from across the world sell modern and contemporary art direct at the Business Design Centre; the 2027 fair is the 39th edition.
events.opNote: Preview Evening is Tuesday 19 January, 5pm to 9pm, from £42.75 in advance. Public hours are 11am to 9pm on Wednesday (Wednesday Late View from 5pm), 11am to 7pm Thursday to Saturday and 11am to 5pm on Sunday. Large bags and rucksacks are not allowed inside; there is a cloakroom.

events.name: MegaCon Live (London)
events.style: Comic and pop-culture convention
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: MegaCon's own weekend pass covers both days for one price rather than paying per day.

events.name: Korea
events.style: Major loan exhibition of Korean art and history
events.whyGo: Korean art at a scale London rarely sees, overlapping the Bayeux Tapestry in the same building for four months - book both for one visit.
events.opNote: Price not yet published - check when booking opens.

events.name: Painting the French Riviera
events.style: Picasso, Matisse and the Cote d'Azur, 1870s-1960s
events.whyGo: Over 160 works - Picasso, Matisse, Cezanne, Renoir - organised with the Cleveland Museum of Art, so this exact loan list will not reassemble.
events.opNote: RA Friends preview 29 September to 1 October; free for Friends throughout.

events.name: Amar Kanwar
events.style: Meditative film installation
events.duration: An hour if you let it work
events.whyGo: Free and built to be sat with rather than lapped - the counterweight to a day of blockbuster queues.
events.opNote: Across the bridge from the Caguiat show; one visit covers both galleries.

events.name: Renoir and Love
events.style: The biggest UK Renoir show in twenty years
events.whyGo: The most significant UK Renoir exhibition in two decades - weekends and holiday dates will sell out, so book rather than stroll up.
events.opNote: Selected Friday evenings run pay-what-you-wish entry. Overlaps Van Eyck in the same building from late November.

events.name: PLATFORM: Simone Brewster
events.style: One designer's practice, free
events.whyGo: The museum's free PLATFORM slot, given to a single contemporary designer - a lower-commitment stop than the ticketed shows upstairs.
events.opNote: Museum publishes the close only as January 2027; the exact day here is provisional.

events.name: Club NVRLND
events.style: Peter Pan as a nightclub musical
events.whyGo: Peter Pan rewritten as a club night, with the cast performing around a dancefloor you are standing on rather than a stage you face.
events.opNote: Runs 14 November 2026 to 31 January 2027. Over-18.

events.name: Tim Walker's Fairyland: Love and Legends
events.style: Fashion photography turned to queer identity and legend
events.whyGo: One of Britain's best-known fashion photographers working well outside his editorial register - queer identity, community and legend rather than campaigns.

events.name: Yinka Shonibare and Thomas Gainsborough: A Conversation
events.style: A single room pairing Gainsborough's Mr and Mrs Andrews with Shonibare's 1998 headless sculpture of the couple in West African textiles
events.venue: National Gallery, H J Hyams Room (Room 1)
events.whyGo: Shonibare removes the heads of the 1750 painting's couple and dresses them in West African textiles, connecting their wealth to the colonial networks that ran through 18th-century Britain.
events.opNote: Until 7 February 2027, free to all visitors.

events.name: The 90s: Art and Fashion
events.style: YBA-era art and 90s British fashion together
events.whyGo: The YBAs and 90s British fashion in one show - a wider lens than the single-medium retrospectives, running through Valentine's week and half term.
events.opNote: Free for Tate Members.

events.name: Cecilia Vicuña: Foraging Quipu
events.style: A gallery presentation of the Chilean artist and poet's quipu works
events.whyGo: Free entry to a long run in Gallery 4, with the gallery open late on Thursdays.
events.opNote: 7 October 2026 to 14 February 2027. Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 11am to 6pm; Thursday 11am to 9pm; closed Mondays.

events.name: Chinese New Year in London
events.style: Europe's largest Lunar New Year celebration - parade, lions, Chinatown shut to traffic
events.venue: Trafalgar Square, Shaftesbury Avenue and Chinatown
events.typicalWhen: The Sunday closest to Lunar New Year, late January to mid-February
events.whyGo: Europe's largest gathering of Chinese lions and dragons parades from Trafalgar Square into a Chinatown closed to traffic for the day. Several hundred thousand people come, so arrive well before the late-morning start.
events.opNote: Lunar New Year 2027 falls on Saturday 6 February; Chinatown's celebrations run 6-20 February. The parade day is set by the London Chinatown Chinese Association.

events.name: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography
events.style: Photography's first claim to be art
events.whyGo: Reaches back to photography's earliest claims to be art - an unusual historical register for Tate Modern.
events.opNote: Pairs with any ticketed show on the same visit.

events.name: London Fashion Week
events.style: The shows are closed; the public fringe is the visitable part
events.typicalWhen: Five days in mid-September and five in mid-to-late February
events.price: Public events free to ticketed; runway shows invitation-only
events.whyGo: Unlike Paris or Milan, London runs a genuine public fringe - designer pop-up sales and British Fashion Council exhibitions alongside the closed shows - so a visitor without an invitation still has something real to do beyond people-watching outside venues.
events.opNote: February 2027 edition runs 18-22 February. The public programme publishes at londonfashionweek.co.uk close to each edition.

events.name: Robert Ryman: The Real Thing
events.style: The white-on-white paintings, in full retrospective
events.whyGo: Ryman's white monochromes divide people like little else in modern painting - a full retrospective is the honest way to decide for yourself.
events.opNote: Fills the whole main gallery; allow longer than a single-room show.

events.name: Motorsport Expo
events.style: 200-plus exhibitors for the racing and motorsport scene
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: Over 200 exhibitors for the racing and motorsport scene specifically, run by CarShowCo alongside Car Culture UK on overlapping dates.
events.opNote: Overlaps Car Culture UK, run by the same organiser, on the same site.

events.name: Car Culture UK
events.style: Modified and custom car culture show
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: Run by CarShowCo alongside Motorsport Expo on overlapping dates at the same venue, aimed at custom and modified car culture rather than racing specifically.
events.opNote: Overlaps Motorsport Expo, run by the same organiser, on the same site.

events.name: Gathering Ground
events.style: Free group show
events.whyGo: Free with a long run into March - the reliable wet-weather fallback at Tate Modern whatever else is on.
events.opNote: No booking pressure; walk in.

events.name: Nan Goldin: You Never Did Anything Wrong
events.style: Full retrospective of the photographer
events.whyGo: A full retrospective of Nan Goldin: addiction, intimacy and the AIDS crisis. The Hayward warns that some work is graphic and sexual, so think twice before bringing children.

events.name: Peggy Guggenheim in London: The Making of a Collector
events.style: How the collection was actually built
events.whyGo: The collector's story rather than the collection's greatest hits - the right show for anyone who has already done the Venice museum.
events.opNote: Runs the whole winter; overlaps French Riviera in the same building through January.

events.name: MOVE IT
events.style: The UK's largest dance exhibition, with a class programme and performances across four stages
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: Billed by its organiser as the UK's largest dance exhibition - a class programme plus performances running across four stages.

events.name: Agentic Expo
events.style: Billed as the first trade exhibition for market-ready AI agents
events.whyGo: The organiser's own billing calls it the world's first trade exhibition for market-ready AI agents, with tickets on open sale rather than gated to trade badges.

events.name: Es Devlin: Other Worlds
events.style: The first European retrospective of Es Devlin's 30-year practice across sculpture, stage design, music, language and light
events.price: Adult from £17.09, concession from £12.82, child from £8.55
events.whyGo: Artworks, installations and film alongside the largest presentation of Devlin's archive so far, including a replica of her London studio filled with her books, objects and maquettes.
events.opNote: 2 October 2026 to 4 April 2027. If your time slot is sold out online, a limited number of tickets may be available from the ticket desk. The museum is closed 24 to 26 December.

events.name: Vanessa Bell & Duncan Grant: Inside Bloomsbury
events.style: The Bloomsbury Group's two central painters
events.whyGo: Bell and Grant carried the Bloomsbury Group's visual side, and the run spans Christmas to spring - a natural tie-in with our Bloomsbury guide.
events.opNote: Free for Tate Members.

events.name: Van Eyck: The Portraits
events.style: The first exhibition ever devoted to Van Eyck's portraiture
events.whyGo: The first show ever devoted to Van Eyck's portraits - an unrepeatable claim, not marketing. Overlaps Renoir in the same building for two months.
events.opNote: Book well ahead for December-January dates.

events.name: Tarek Atoui: Hyundai Commission
events.style: The Turbine Hall commission, built from sound
events.whyGo: The Turbine Hall commission is always free and always at a scale nothing else in London matches - this year's is built around sound.
events.opNote: Walk in; the hall is the museum's front door.

events.name: Ideal Home Show
events.style: The UK's biggest home, garden and lifestyle consumer show
events.whyGo: A long-running annual fixture at Olympia, and the UK's biggest consumer show for the home, garden and lifestyle by its own billing.
events.opNote: The 2026 edition ran 10-19 April; 2027 dates are confirmed directly on the organiser's own site.

events.name: Ossie Clark + Celia Birtwell
events.style: The designs and prints of the fashion and textile duo who shaped 1960s and early 1970s fashion
events.whyGo: Explores the life and work of Ossie Clark and the textile prints of Celia Birtwell, with a book published alongside on 2 October.
events.opNote: 2 October 2026 to 11 April 2027. Open Tuesday to Saturday, 11am to 6pm, last entry 5.15pm; closed Sundays and Mondays, and reopening after the Christmas break on Saturday 2 January.

events.name: Peter Blake: In the Studio
events.style: A major exhibition on the life and work of Sir Peter Blake, with recent collages responding to William Hogarth
events.whyGo: Seven decades of work by Peter Blake, the Pop artist who co-designed the cover of the Beatles' Sgt. Pepper album.
events.opNote: 25 November 2026 to 18 April 2027. Tickets cover the whole run; book ahead for weekends and festive and school holiday periods.

events.name: Secret Cinema Presents Pirates of the Caribbean
events.style: Film screening inside a built world
events.whyGo: Secret Cinema's format: a full set built around the film, actors in it, and you in costume before the screening starts.
events.opNote: 16 February to 25 April 2027 - the furthest ahead on this list. Costume is expected rather than optional.

events.name: Grand Designs Live (London)
events.style: The TV show's live build, design and self-build exhibition
events.typicalWhen: Late April to early May, annually
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.price: From about £16 adult on the day; under-16s free
events.whyGo: The organiser, Media 10, runs the NEC Birmingham edition first each autumn; this is the London date that follows it.
events.opNote: The price is the NEC Birmingham October 2026 edition's on-the-day rate; London prices its own show closer to the date.

events.name: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires
events.style: Art and design from the city across more than a thousand years, in Galleries 38 and 39
events.whyGo: Art and design from more than a thousand years of Constantinople and Istanbul, under the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.
events.opNote: Closes Sunday 9 May 2027. Advance booking recommended. V&A members have unlimited free entry to exhibitions.

events.name: Tove Jansson and her Families
events.style: The UK's first exhibition of Tove Jansson's original works in almost a decade, on the people who shaped her life and work
events.whyGo: Original illustrations and works by the creator of the Moomins, looking at the families, chosen and by birth, around the Finnish artist-author (1914 to 2001).
events.opNote: 21 November 2026 to 9 May 2027, Wednesday to Sunday 10am to 5pm. A ticket includes all current exhibitions; members go free. A Moomins-inspired festive late is on Thursday 10 December.

events.name: London Coffee Festival
events.style: Four days of coffee, tastings and barista competition at the Truman Brewery
events.typicalWhen: Four days in mid-May - trade days first, public weekend after
events.whyGo: About 275 coffee and food brands fill the old brewery, with the Coffee Masters competition running through the trade days. A reliable preview of what turns up in London's actual cafes over the following year.
events.opNote: 13-16 May 2027 confirmed on the festival's own site; tickets not yet on sale at the time of checking.

events.name: MCM Comic Con London
events.style: The organiser's own billing calls it the UK's biggest Comic Con
events.typicalWhen: Two editions a year, at ExCeL in May and October
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.price: Priority entry from £39; tickets on sale from 26 October 2026
events.whyGo: Billed by its organiser as the UK's biggest Comic Con; the Weekend ticket and both VIP tiers sold out more than a month before the October 2026 show.
events.opNote: EGX, RX's sister gaming show, has been folded into this London date - egx.net now lists only MCM London and MCM Birmingham.

events.name: U2: The Greatest Show On Earth World Tour
events.style: Two stadium nights with Wolf Alice supporting, the tour's only UK venue
events.whyGo: U2 play Friday 18 and Saturday 19 June 2027 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which the stadium lists as the only UK venue on the tour. Wolf Alice support.
events.opNote: General sale opens at 10am on Friday 6 November 2026, for reserved seating, standing and VIP packages. U2.com presales run from Monday 2 November, and the artist presale is on Thursday 5 November. Accessible tickets need Nimbus Disability Access Scheme registration before booking.

events.name: Agatha Christie: A World of Mystery
events.style: Christie's life and travels, from a WWI dispensary to an Orient Express-style carriage
events.price: £25 at peak; £20 off-peak to 21 February 2027, then £23
events.whyGo: Rooms styled as a country house, a WWI dispensary, an Orient Express-style carriage, an archaeological dig and a West End theatre, with Christie's 1937 Remington typewriter, early manuscripts, notebooks and letters.
events.opNote: Peak is Saturdays, Sundays, bank holidays and the last month of the run, from Monday 24 May 2027. Off-peak tickets rise from £20 to £23 on 22 February 2027. Concessions for under-16s, 16 to 25s, students, disabled people and carers; members go free; Universal Credit and Pension Credit recipients pay £3 off-peak.

events.name: Monet: Painting Time
events.style: A major Monet retrospective on light and time
events.whyGo: Monet blockbusters sell out months ahead and readers plan trips around them - flagged now even though it opens in February 2027.
events.opNote: Booking will open well before the February opening; free for Tate Members.

events.name: The Bayeux Tapestry
events.style: The Tapestry's first time out of France in nearly a millennium
events.whyGo: The actual Bayeux Tapestry, leaving France for the first time in nearly a thousand years. The single biggest cultural loan London has hosted in decades, and the one exhibition this year to plan a trip around.
events.opNote: Opens 10 September 2026 and runs to July 2027. Expect the tightest booking of anything on this page.

events.name: Wildlife Photographer of the Year
events.style: The winning images from the Natural History Museum's annual nature photography competition
events.whyGo: The 62nd Wildlife Photographer of the Year: the winning photographs, each shown with the story behind the picture.
events.opNote: Off-peak is Tuesday to Thursday in term time; peak is weekends in the school holidays. Under-4s free. Central Building, Natural History Museum.

events.name: Doggett's Coat and Badge Race
events.style: The oldest continuously held annual sporting event in the world
events.venue: The Thames, London Bridge to Cadogan Pier
events.typicalWhen: One afternoon in late summer - the month has drifted between July and September, so check
events.duration: About half an hour to pass any one point
events.whyGo: Single scullers race four miles and seven furlongs from London Bridge to Chelsea for a scarlet coat and silver badge, as they have since 1715 - older than the Boat Race and the Derby. Watch free from any bridge on the route.
events.opNote: The 312th running starts 1.15pm on 2 September 2026. Organised by the Fishmongers' and Watermen's Companies, who have never needed to market it - which is why almost nobody watching knows what they are seeing.

events.name: Totally Thames
events.style: A month of river-themed events across twenty boroughs
events.venue: Along the Thames, Richmond to Barking
events.whyGo: Over a hundred river events under one umbrella - foreshore walks, boat festivals, art installations - that absorbed the old Mayor's Thames Festival. A September visit can be built around it without realising it is one programme.
events.opNote: Most events free and unticketed. Highlights in 2026 include Chiswick Tidefest on 6 September and the St Katharine Docks Classic Boat Festival on 12-13 September.

events.name: The Great River Race
events.style: 300 traditional boats racing 21.6 miles through all of London's bridges
events.address: Start at Millwall, finish at Ham
events.duration: An hour or so at any one bridge
events.whyGo: Gigs, skiffs, dragon boats and Celtic longboats - about 300 of them, from serious clubs to fancy-dress novelty crews - race under all 28 bridges between the Docklands and Richmond. The best day of the year to lean on a bridge and watch the river.
events.opNote: Free from any bridge or bank on the route. It runs upstream with the tide, so check the start time to work out when it reaches your stretch.

events.name: Open House Festival
events.style: 800+ normally closed buildings open free across every borough
events.typicalWhen: A week to ten days in mid-September
events.duration: As many buildings as you can fit
events.whyGo: The one week a year you can walk into the Lloyd's Building, private livery halls and architects' own homes for nothing. The 2026 programme marks the Lloyd's Building's 40th birthday.
events.opNote: Most buildings are walk-in but the famous ones are ticketed ballots that open weeks ahead and fill within hours - plan those first. 2026 booking opened 19 August.

events.name: London Design Festival
events.style: City-wide design festival across eleven design districts
events.venue: Design districts city-wide, plus the V&A and Design Museum
events.typicalWhen: Mid-to-late September, the same week as Open House
events.address: Districts include Bankside, Brompton, Shoreditch and Chelsea
events.whyGo: Eleven design districts run trails, installations and open studios, with the V&A and Design Museum programming their own strands rather than hosting incidentally. It rewards picking one neighbourhood over trying to see all of it.
events.opNote: Runs the same week as Open House London, so architecture and design combine into one dense week. Talks and forums book up; the district trails are walk-in.

events.name: BFI London Film Festival
events.style: The UK's biggest public film festival
events.venue: BFI Southbank and cinemas across the West End
events.whyGo: Unlike Cannes or Venice, anyone can buy a ticket to the premieres - no accreditation, just booking speed. The 2026 edition is the 70th.
events.opNote: Public booking opens in September and the galas go fast; ordinary screenings of the same films are far easier to get.

events.name: Frieze London and Frieze Sculpture
events.style: Contemporary art fair, with a free outdoor sculpture park alongside
events.typicalWhen: The fair is five days in mid-October; the free sculpture runs mid-September to the start of November
events.duration: An hour for the sculpture, half a day for the fair
events.price: Sculpture free; the fair is ticketed
events.whyGo: The ticketed fair gets the coverage, but Frieze Sculpture is the half guides miss - six weeks of large-scale outdoor work in the English Gardens, free, no ticket. The fair itself runs 15-18 October 2026.
events.opNote: Dates span the free sculpture run; the fair is 14 October (invitation preview) then public 15-18 October.

events.name: Diwali on the Square
events.style: The Mayor of London's free Diwali festival
events.typicalWhen: A Sunday in October or November, moving with the Hindu lunar calendar
events.whyGo: London's biggest single Diwali gathering, around 35,000 people, with the Mayor lighting the ceremonial lamp. City-hall-run and completely free, like Eid and Vaisakhi on the same square.
events.opNote: 2026 edition confirmed for Sunday 25 October, 1pm-7pm. No ticket, just turn up.

events.name: Eid on the Square
events.style: The Mayor of London's free Eid al-Adha festival
events.typicalWhen: Moves with the Islamic lunar calendar, roughly eleven days earlier each year - it fell on 30 May in 2026
events.whyGo: Twenty years running, and deliberately plural - Turkish, Middle Eastern, Malaysian, Indonesian, North African and South Asian communities share one stage rather than a single homogenous Eid. BSL interpretation and access are built in.
events.opNote: The 2026 edition ran 30 May. The 2027 date will fall roughly eleven days earlier and is not yet published - do not guess it.

events.name: Trooping the Colour
events.style: The King's official birthday parade - massed bands, cavalry, RAF flypast
events.venue: Horse Guards Parade and The Mall
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in mid-June, with full dress rehearsals the two Saturdays before
events.price: Free from The Mall; stand seats by ballot
events.whyGo: The parade everyone knows - the useful detail is the two rehearsals on the preceding Saturdays. The Major General's Review and the Colonel's Review are near-identical dress rehearsals with a fraction of the crowd.
events.opNote: 2026 ran 13 June with rehearsals 30 May and 6 June. 2027 date not yet announced; the mid-June Saturday pattern holds.

events.name: Royal Gun Salutes
events.style: The King's Troop gallops six guns across Hyde Park and fires a 41-gun salute
events.venue: Hyde Park or Green Park, and the Tower of London
events.typicalWhen: Fixed royal dates every year: 6 May, the King's official birthday in June, 8 September and 14 November, plus state occasions
events.whyGo: Horse-drawn guns arrive at the gallop, fire blank rounds at ten-second intervals, and leave - dramatic, free, and unknown to most visitors because it is never marketed as an event. The Tower fires 62 rounds the same day.
events.opNote: Recurs on the same handful of dates every year, which makes it one of the easiest free spectacles to plan around. Hyde Park salutes usually fire at noon - check royal.uk for each date.

events.name: The Knollys Rose Ceremony
events.style: One red rose, carried in procession, paid to the Lord Mayor as 645-year-old rent
events.venue: Seething Lane garden to Mansion House
events.whyGo: Sir Robert Knolles built a footbridge without permission in 1381 and the fine - one red rose a year - is still being paid, in person, in procession. Revived in 1924 and performed to almost no audience at all.
events.opNote: A weekday in late June, unticketed and barely publicised. Check the Company of Watermen or City events listings for the exact date.

events.name: Pearly Kings and Queens Harvest Festival
events.style: The Pearlies in full button suits - procession, maypole and a harvest church service
events.typicalWhen: A Sunday in late September, from early afternoon
events.whyGo: Thousands of hand-sewn buttons, 150 years of costermonger tradition, morris dancing in Guildhall Yard and a working church service at St Mary-le-Bow. As visually distinctive as Carnival with a fraction of the attention.
events.opNote: A parade from Guildhall Yard to a harvest service at St Mary-le-Bow.

events.name: St Patrick's Day Parade and Festival
events.style: Free Irish parade to a Trafalgar Square stage festival
events.venue: Hyde Park Corner to Trafalgar Square
events.whyGo: More than 50,000 people watch bands from the UK, Ireland and the US process a mile and a half to a full afternoon of live Irish music in Trafalgar Square. Mayor-produced, so free start to finish.

events.name: The Boat Race
events.style: Oxford v Cambridge on the Championship Course, free from the bank
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in late March or early April - the date follows the tides
events.duration: The race passes in minutes; the day is an afternoon
events.whyGo: The crowded spots are Putney at the start and Hammersmith Bridge; Barnes Bridge near the finish is far less mobbed and the race is usually still alive there. Free the whole four and a quarter miles.
events.opNote: Exact date announced each year once tides are known. The towpath pubs fill hours ahead.

events.name: Head of the River Race
events.style: 400+ eights race the Boat Race course in procession
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in mid-to-late March, usually just before the Boat Race
events.whyGo: The same stretch of river as the Boat Race but with several hundred crews instead of two - a far better spectacle for anyone who wants to watch rowing rather than a rivalry. Nothing to book because there is nothing to buy.
events.opNote: Run with the ebb tide, Mortlake down to Putney. Any towpath spot works.

events.name: The Championships, Wimbledon
events.style: The Grand Slam, and The Queue is the walk-up route nobody believes exists
events.typicalWhen: Two weeks, late June into early July
events.price: Grounds passes from roughly £30; show courts by ballot
events.whyGo: The one genuinely useful fact: The Queue is a real same-day walk-up route to grounds tickets that needs no ballot - arrive early, queue on the grass, and you are in. Most first-time visitors have no idea it exists.
events.opNote: Show courts go by public ballot months ahead. The Queue starts the night before for the biggest days; a weekday-morning arrival usually gets a grounds pass.

events.name: All Points East
events.style: Two festival weekends in Victoria Park
events.price: From £84.95 plus booking for general admission (Phoebe Bridgers, 27 August 2027)
events.whyGo: The east London festival that stayed put while Lovebox and Field Day moved on, now two full weekends. The 2026 second weekend was headlined by Lorde and Tyler, the Creator.
events.opNote: Single-day tickets per headliner rather than camping. 2027 opens on Friday 27 August with Phoebe Bridgers, Caroline Polachek, Kelsey Lu, Danielle Ponder and jasmine.4.t; tickets are on sale.

events.name: BST Hyde Park
events.style: Stadium-scale single-day concerts in Hyde Park
events.typicalWhen: Headline Saturdays and Sundays from late June through mid-July
events.price: From £105.95 plus fees (Bon Jovi, Thursday 24 June 2027)
events.whyGo: One massive act per ticket, in central London, and back at your hotel by midnight - no tent, no fields. Lineups announce only a few months out, so it suits shorter-lead planning.
events.opNote: Between headline days the site runs Open House - free midweek entry to the arena with screens, bars and food. Worth knowing if you are in the park anyway.

events.name: Camden Fringe
events.style: 400+ fringe shows across small Camden venues every August
events.venue: Etcetera Theatre, Camden People's Theatre and a dozen more
events.whyGo: The same density of new stand-up and theatre as Edinburgh every August, without the flight or the hotel prices - performers use it to preview the material they take north. Over 400 shows in 2025.
events.opNote: Programme publishes in early summer at camdenfringe.com. Most venues are pub theatres under 60 seats, so book the buzzy shows.

events.name: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
events.style: The world's most famous flower show, rebuilt from bare ground each May
events.typicalWhen: Five days in the third week of May - the first two are RHS members only
events.price: All tickets advance-only; roughly £30-£100+ by day
events.whyGo: An 11-acre site built from nothing every spring, shown for five days and dismantled within a week - about 157,000 people see it. Monday and Tuesday are members-only, which catches out anyone trying to book blind.
events.opNote: Book months ahead; the Friday and Saturday sell out first. The Sell-Off on the final afternoon, when exhibitors sell the actual plants, is the insider hour.

events.name: Meltdown
events.style: A festival programmed by a different guest artist every year
events.typicalWhen: 10 to 20 June 2027 (around ten days in June each year)
events.whyGo: A single curator books the whole festival, so the line-up changes completely each year. FKA twigs curates 2027.
events.opNote: Has skipped years before (2006, 2020-21), so confirm the current edition exists before planning around it.

events.name: Taste of London
events.style: London's restaurants serve taster menus in Regent's Park
events.price: Entry from about £24, then pay per dish
events.whyGo: Dozens of real London restaurants serve small plates of their actual menus, so it works as a tasting flight of places you would otherwise book one by one. Friday sessions have historically had free children's entry.
events.opNote: Entry ticket plus pay-as-you-eat inside.

events.name: EFG London Jazz Festival
events.style: Ten days of jazz from the Barbican to pub back rooms
events.venue: Venues city-wide, anchored at the Southbank Centre
events.price: Free fringe gigs up to £50+ headline concerts
events.whyGo: The same ten days span £60 Barbican headliners and £10 pub sessions, and the free fringe strand is the part visitor guides always skip. Programming runs across the small rooms in our live music guide.
events.opNote: Programme publishes around September at efglondonjazzfestival.org.uk. The famous names sell out; the discovery gigs do not.

events.name: Remembrance Sunday at the Cenotaph
events.style: The national act of remembrance, and the veterans' march-past after it
events.typicalWhen: The second Sunday in November, silence at 11am
events.duration: The morning, with the march-past continuing after
events.whyGo: The two-minute silence is the famous part; the veterans' march-past afterwards - thousands walking past the Cenotaph by association, for hours - is far less crowded to watch and at least as affecting.
events.opNote: Whitehall fills early for the ceremony itself. Arriving late morning for the march-past is the quieter way in.

events.name: Jack in the Green, Deptford
events.style: A giant leaf-covered Jack paraded through Deptford with morris sides and drums
events.typicalWhen: May Day - 1 May or the nearest bank holiday weekend
events.whyGo: Fowlers Troop parade one of the tallest Jack in the Green figures in the country through streets no tourist visits, reviving a pagan May tradition that died out in Victorian London. No tickets, no marketing - you find it by knowing it exists.
events.opNote: Route and timing vary year to year and publish quietly. Deptford High Street mid-morning on the day is the safe bet.

events.name: London Mela
events.style: One of Europe's largest South Asian festivals, free in Gunnersbury Park
events.typicalWhen: A weekend in late August or early September
events.whyGo: Six-figure weekend attendance and barely a mention in mainstream round-ups - music, dance and food across one of Europe's biggest Melas. Gunnersbury Park and its museum are worth the trip on their own.
events.opNote: Free and unticketed. Check londonmela.org for the current year before travelling - the date moves within late summer.

events.name: West End Live
events.style: Casts of the current West End shows perform free in Trafalgar Square
events.whyGo: Full numbers from whatever is running in the West End, performed by the actual casts on an outdoor stage, for nothing. The programme is exactly as good as that year's theatre season.
events.opNote: Unticketed and rammed - the square reaches capacity by late morning, so go early to a specific show slot. Run by Westminster and the Society of London Theatre.

events.name: London Cocktail Week
events.style: One wristband, discounted signature cocktails at hundreds of bars
events.typicalWhen: Around ten days in early-to-mid October
events.duration: As many bars as you can manage
events.whyGo: The format is the draw: one wristband works at several hundred independent bars, which turns it into a self-guided crawl through neighbourhoods you would not otherwise hit in one trip. Pairs naturally with our cocktail bars guide.
events.opNote: Buy the wristband online ahead. Signature serves are discounted, not free.

events.name: Battle of Britain Anniversary Flypast
events.style: Historic RAF aircraft low over central London, free and barely publicised
events.venue: Over central London; service at Westminster Abbey
events.address: Best viewed from The Mall and Westminster
events.whyGo: A Spitfire and Hurricane from the Memorial Flight pass low over central London on the Sunday nearest the anniversary, with no publicity beyond RAF and Abbey channels. Most people who see it have no idea it happens every year.
events.opNote: Timing publishes quietly via the RAF; The Mall and the bridges give the clearest sightlines.

events.name: Shrove Tuesday Pancake Races
events.style: Fancy-dress relay races flipping pancakes, at several spots across town
events.typicalWhen: Shrove Tuesday - 47 days before Easter, February or early March
events.address: Old Spitalfields Market and other locations
events.whyGo: Teams in fancy dress flip pancakes down a marked course for a crowd of about a hundred - small, silly, and genuinely local rather than staged. The Spitalfields race is the reliable central one.
events.opNote: Shrove Tuesday 2027 falls on 9 February. Individual races publish quietly - check Old Spitalfields Market's events page.

events.name: Beating Retreat
events.style: Massed bands, cannon and drill at dusk on Horse Guards Parade
events.typicalWhen: Two evenings in June, just before Trooping the Colour
events.whyGo: The evening version of Trooping the Colour almost nobody outside London mentions - pipes, drums, cannon and cavalry at dusk, with a senior royal taking the salute. Ticketed, which keeps it far smaller than the parade itself.
events.opNote: Tickets via the Household Division; the two evenings differ slightly in programme.

events.name: Winter Lights
events.style: Free outdoor light-art trail
events.typicalWhen: Second half of January, nightly from about 5pm to 10pm
events.whyGo: Around twenty light installations by international artists, spread across the estate and the dockside after dark, free and with no ticket. The 2026 edition was the tenth.
events.opNote: No booking and no entry point - it is a self-guided trail across the whole estate, so arrive at any stop. Busiest at weekends; a weekday evening is much quieter.

events.name: Larger Than Life: Starring Wallace & Gromit
events.style: Aardman sets, models and animation
events.whyGo: Aardman's actual sets and models up close, where you can see the thumbprints left in the plasticine.
events.opNote: OPENS 14 OCTOBER 2026 - not open yet. No published closing date.

events.name: Phantom Peak
events.style: Open-world town you explore at your own pace
events.whyGo: A whole built town with more than twenty parallel storylines running at once - you pick which to follow and cannot see them all in one visit.
events.opNote: Opens on 12 February 2027 at Westfield Stratford City, with tickets on sale. The original Canada Water venue closed on 28 February 2026 after 625 performances.

events.name: Notting Hill Carnival
events.style: Europe's largest street carnival
events.whyGo: Two million people, Europe's biggest street carnival, led by London's Caribbean communities since 1966 - sound systems, mas bands and steel pan through the streets of W11, and free.
events.opNote: SUNDAY IS FAMILY DAY and much calmer than Monday. Ladbroke Grove and Westbourne Park stations go exit-only or shut entirely - plan the walk out before you go in.

events.name: The London Marathon
events.style: Mass-participation marathon through the city
events.whyGo: Free to watch and one of the great days in the London calendar - the start is on Blackheath, and the course runs through Greenwich, Tower Bridge and Canary Wharf to The Mall.
events.opNote: FREE TO WATCH but it closes a great many roads and the DLR and Jubilee line are packed all morning. Greenwich around the 10km mark is one of the best and loudest stretches.

events.name: Pride in London
events.style: Parade and stages across central London
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in late June or early July
events.whyGo: The parade runs through the middle of town to Whitehall, and Soho - which is the reason Pride is here at all - becomes one continuous street party for the day.
events.opNote: Free. Soho is closed to traffic and rammed; Old Compton Street is the centre of it. Trafalgar Square and Golden Square hold the free stages.

events.name: The Lord Mayor's Show
events.style: A procession that has run since 1215
events.address: Mansion House to the Royal Courts of Justice
events.duration: A morning, with fireworks at dusk
events.whyGo: A procession that has run every year since 1215 - state coach, livery companies, floats and a river of marching bands through the Square Mile, followed by fireworks on the Thames.
events.opNote: Free and one of the oldest civic events in the world. Get a spot on Cheapside or Fleet Street early; the fireworks are from the river at dusk.

events.name: The BBC Proms
events.style: Eight weeks of concerts, standing tickets from a few pounds
events.whyGo: Eight weeks of world-class orchestral music where you can stand in the arena for the price of a pint - the Promming tickets are the whole point and are sold on the day.
events.opNote: PROMMING TICKETS ARE SOLD ON THE DAY and cannot be booked - queue at the hall. Everything else books months ahead. The Last Night is balloted.

events.name: Bonfire Night Fireworks
events.style: Firework displays across the city
events.address: Victoria Park and parks across London
events.price: Free to ticketed depending on the display
events.whyGo: Displays across the big parks and clubs on the weekend nearest the fifth of November; the big ones are Alexandra Palace and Battersea Park.
events.opNote: No London borough council still funds a free public display, and the one free display (Coram's Fields, 5 November) is for children and the adults with them. Check the individual display.

events.name: Greenwich Fair
events.style: Free street theatre, circus and family entertainment
events.typicalWhen: August bank holiday weekend, as part of the Greenwich+Docklands International Festival
events.address: General Wolfe Piazza, Observatory Hill, Greenwich Park
events.whyGo: Two free afternoons of street theatre, circus, puppetry and acrobatics at the top of Greenwich Park - the closing weekend of GDIF, and small enough to still feel like a local fete rather than a festival.
events.opNote: No booking - just turn up. A level access route runs from the Blackheath Gate (about 15 minutes); the step-free route from St Mary's Gate is uphill and takes 10-15 minutes.

events.name: North End Road Summer Festival
events.style: Traffic-free street festival on a Victorian market street
events.whyGo: North End Road's market has traded six days a week since the 1880s; once a year the council closes it to traffic and adds 150-plus stalls, live music, street entertainers and free kids' workshops on top of the regular fruit-and-veg traders.
events.opNote: 10am-6pm, free, no booking. Award-winning as a community market (Best Community/Parish Market, Great British Market Awards 2019) - genuinely council-run rather than a private promotion.

events.name: Summer Sounds
events.style: Free open-air live music
events.typicalWhen: Mid-to-late August, over about ten days
events.whyGo: Ten days of free live music outdoors by the fountains at Granary Square - no ticket, no booking, and one of the better free things London puts on in August.
events.opNote: Free and unticketed, so it gets busy at the front. The canal steps behind the square are the sensible place to sit. Dates shift slightly each year.

events.name: The Classic Car Boot Sale
events.style: Vintage traders, classic cars and street food
events.venue: Granary Square, Lewis Cubitt Square and Coal Drops Yard
events.typicalWhen: Twice a year - a spring edition around April and an autumn one in September
events.address: Granary Square and Lewis Cubitt Square
events.whyGo: Over a hundred vintage traders and seventy-odd classic cars spread across three King's Cross squares, plus the UK's largest open-air Charity Super.Mkt. It passed its tenth year at King's Cross in 2025.
events.opNote: Runs 10am to 6pm across two days, and happens TWICE a year rather than once - check which edition is next before planning around it.

events.name: Affordable Art Fair - Battersea Autumn
events.style: Collector-entry art fair, aimed at first-time buyers rather than blue-chip galleries
events.whyGo: One of Frieze Week's satellite fairs, priced and pitched at collectors buying their first piece rather than six-figure lots.
events.opNote: Private view Wednesday 14 October, 5-9pm; general admission runs Thursday 15 to Sunday 18 October.

events.name: 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair
events.style: Contemporary African and diaspora galleries filling Somerset House's wings and courtyard
events.whyGo: Its 14th edition, and the one Frieze Week fair built entirely around African and diaspora galleries rather than a general survey.
events.opNote: 15 October is a ticketed press and VIP preview; public days are 16 to 18 October.

events.name: AnimeCon London
events.style: Anime, manga, J-Pop, K-Pop and fashion over two days
events.whyGo: Billed by its organiser, the Oakham Group, as the UK's biggest anime and manga convention.
events.opNote: In the Grand Hall.

events.name: Musical Con
events.style: West End cast meet-and-greets, workshops and masterclasses
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: West End cast meet-and-greets and workshops are sold as separate add-ons on top of entry, and several tiers were already marked sold out on the organiser's own ticket page.

events.name: New Scientist Live
events.style: Four stages of talks and a show floor, livestreamed for ticket holders
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: Four stages and 47-plus speakers on one show floor; the organiser's own site advertises up to 44% off its final-release tickets against paying on the door.
events.opNote: 10-11 October are the public days; 12 October is a Schools' Day, not open to the public.

events.name: AI LIVE
events.style: AI industry talks and a show floor
events.whyGo: Labelled a trade show on Olympia's own listing, but openly ticketed with no business-email gate found on the organiser's site.

events.name: Home, Life & You LIVE
events.style: Home, lifestyle and gardening exhibitors and demonstrations
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: Home, lifestyle and gardening exhibitors and demonstrations on the same October weekend as the National Wedding Show and Musical Con at the same venue.
events.opNote: Ticket price not published on the organiser's own site.

events.name: Vegan Life Live / OM Yoga Show / Mind Body Soul Experience
events.style: Three co-located shows on one ticket: plant-based food, yoga and wellbeing
events.whyGo: One entrance ticket covers all three co-located shows, and under-16s go free with a paying adult.

events.name: Knit + Stitch
events.style: 300-plus specialist textile craft suppliers under one roof
events.whyGo: The venue's own billing calls it the UK's biggest textile craft exhibition, with over 300 specialist suppliers under one roof.

events.name: Open Studios (Muswell Hill & Alexandra Park)
events.style: Seventy-plus local artists open their own studios for the weekend
events.venue: Alexandra Palace (Creativity Pavilion) and artists' own studios
events.whyGo: Free, and the second year of Muswell Hill and Alexandra Park artists opening their own studios rather than showing in a single hall.
events.opNote: The Creativity Pavilion at Alexandra Palace is the starting point; the rest of the trail runs across artists' own studios nearby.

events.name: The National Wedding Show
events.style: Wedding suppliers and showcases under one roof
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.whyGo: Wedding suppliers and showcases under one roof, on the same weekend as Musical Con and Home, Life & You LIVE at the same venue.
events.opNote: Ticket price not published on the organiser's own site.

events.name: The Luxury Travel Fair
events.style: High-end travel operators and destinations under one roof
events.whyGo: High-end tour operators and destinations under one roof, in the National Hall rather than Olympia's larger main floor.

events.name: What University? & What Career? Live
events.style: University and career fair for school leavers
events.whyGo: Free entry to a university and careers fair for school leavers, in the National Hall.

events.name: UK Black Business Week & Show
events.style: A week of Black-owned business networking, awards and a public show day
events.address: One Western Gateway, Royal Victoria Dock
events.price: Day Pass: Early Bird £45, Pre-Reg £50, Onsite £65
events.whyGo: The public-ticketed day is Saturday 17 October; the rest of the week runs on delegate passes for the Awards, Forum and networking parties.
events.opNote: Public Day Pass runs 9am-6pm on the Saturday only.

events.name: The Baby Show
events.style: Pregnancy through to toddler care, exhibitors and talks
events.whyGo: Pregnancy through to toddler care in one hall, running the same weekend as MCM Comic Con at ExCeL across town.

events.name: London Snow Show
events.style: Ski and snowsports consumer show
events.whyGo: A ski and snowsports consumer show in the National Hall, the same October weekend as the National Wedding Show and Musical Con at ExCeL.
events.opNote: Ticket price not published on the organiser's own listing.

events.name: Spirit of Christmas Fair
events.style: Festive shopping fair for independent businesses
events.whyGo: Festive shopping, independent businesses and food, in the Grand Hall well ahead of the Christmas rush.
